Flex.revenue_growth: CPI $2.2B (+35% YoY), 9.7% op margin; total revenue $7.9B (+21%), op profit $534M
Flex.backlog_or_b2b: EPC'S 2027 IS ALREADY BOOKED, AND A JULY GRID EVENT IS PULLING DEMAND FORWARD (Chris): asked what drives EPC's growth, 'It is all pinned to the data centers. It is all pinned to some of those regulatory requirements that are coming. There is also some tailwinds from bans on foreign-produced product in the critical infrastructure here in the U.S. EPC is all U.S.-based production, so that plays in very well.' Asked about visibility: 'Most of that business is booked today' and 'Really good backlog for 2027.' A specific catalyst was named: 'There was a pretty significant power disturbance in Northern Virginia back in the month of July, and that is driving more utilities to demand this type of technology in the data center.' Margin uplift is attributed to capacity that 'just came online in the month of June', supply-chain reshoring initiatives, and the fact that 'data center margins are a little bit higher than what their traditional business has been.'

Vertiv.supply_status: Albertazzi narrows the supply-chain congestion flagged on the Q2 call: it was not a generic situation but specifically referred to the converged infrastructure products OneCore and SmartRun, where Vertiv is industrializing something that is a field project and taking construction-site complexity onto itself. The consequences are coordination across multiple factories rather than component shortage, and timing variability - is revenue recognized this day or maybe four days later because some of the components are converging in the integration factory. Integration at this scale is a different capability than the power-module integration Vertiv has done for 25, 30 years, and that integration capacity is being deployed constantly to follow demand. He adds the current outlook already incorporates wiggle room against possible hiccups. Chamberlin separately points back to the ramp in infrastructure-solutions orders (Vertiv SmartRun / Vertiv OneCore) seen in last fourth quarter as evidence of the share gain.
Vertiv.next_catalyst: sidecar acceleration in 2027, probably second half of 2027; native end-to-end 800 volt DC powertrain commercially back end of 2027, volumes 2028

Delta Electronics.supply_status: Component supply is tight across the board: lead times are stretching and MOSFETs in particular are short, though Delta's purchasing scale and supplier relationships keep demand largely fulfilled. Memory was the hardest hit - one business unit could not secure memory volumes at workable prices, so it switched designs to second sources and expects H2 shipments to normalize and catch up the backlog without a loss. On wide-bandgap devices (silicon carbide, gallium nitride) Delta works early and closely with the most important suppliers, keeps talking with them continuously and gets early access to new products, but will not disclose any agreements; it is also broadening its supply chain, including Taiwanese supplier options. Supplier price increases will be negotiated and passed to customers where the business model allows, with a timing lag.

Hubei DOTI Micro Technology.guidance: 2026 business plan (annual report): the company calls communications optics its core strategic segment. In 2026 it will focus on ramping optical isolator capacity and yield (expanding capacity by optimising lines and adding staff), move WDM filters, Z-block assemblies, prisms and optical assemblies from sampling to volume shipment and raise their share of communications revenue, and invest in components for 1.6T/3.2T modules (higher-performance WDM filters, more integrated and miniaturised Z-blocks) and in Faraday rotator materials (crystal preparation). It will advance the Nanchang base, adjusting the expansion pace for isolators and spin-coated filters to demand; in imaging it will defend its spin-coated filter share and build the phone micro-prism line. It says global Faraday rotator supply is tight and China's rare-earth export controls widen the gap; it has contingency plans and is cultivating diversified supply. Management says it is confident and that the dual-engine pattern is expected to lift overall results to a new level.
Hubei DOTI Micro Technology.supply_status: Management (IR record; general manager, CFO): Faraday rotators come mainly from overseas, with Japanese makers among the main global suppliers; isolators are currently made mainly with overseas mainstream suppliers' rotators. The company has long-term cooperation with core upstream suppliers; purchasing and production scheduling are normal and operations have not been directly hurt by the policies so far. It hedges rotator price rises through long-term volume and price agreements and stocking, and does not grow rotator crystals itself, though a subsidiary slices, polishes and coats them. Some core customers set terms in mid- to long-term orders, but not all orders are price-locked.

eMemory.revenue_growth: revenue TWD 1,097 million (+0.2% QoQ, +17.1% YoY); operating income TWD 666 million; operating margin 60.7%; net income TWD 580 million (+44.9% YoY); EPS TWD 7.77
eMemory.guidance: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: royalty revenue is expected to accelerate in Q3 and the second half of 2026 - several advanced-node products, including ADAS, AI accelerators, SSDs and networking, have begun entering mass production, and foundry wafer prices are gradually increasing. Chairman Charles Hsu: licensing will continue its strong momentum; royalty growth is expected to accelerate on higher ASP from new advanced-node applications, new application ramps, an expanding PUF royalty contribution and a growing mix of higher-royalty-rate MTP applications.
eMemory.supply_status: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: Q2 royalty corresponds to foundry production in Q1, when mature-node foundry capacity utilization remained at a relatively low level and some customers went through seasonal inventory adjustment; from Q2 overall foundry capacity utilization began to improve.
eMemory.next_catalyst: Chairman Charles Hsu: 1T Flash (NeoFlash / Logic Flash) is in platform development and verification with several foundry partners, each progressing according to plan; customers may begin mass production next year. Standalone development focuses first on NOR Flash; after foundry partners bring standalone NOR Flash into mass production, eMemory may extend 1T Flash into a NAND Flash architecture.
